text:
rahul: Quick perf dump from the multi-model co-residency run on the 4xA100 pool. Seeing reproducible OOM spikes when model-B is loaded while model-A KV cache is hot.

rahul: Profiler attach (short):
```
[prof] timeline: batch_fill -> kernel_select -> allocate_workspace -> kvcache_lookup
[mem] total_gpu: 40GB, used: 36.4GB, free: 3.6GB
[kernel] selected: aten::fwd_opt (workspace 2.1GB) fallback: aten::fwd_stable (workspace 1.8GB)
[oom] events: 3 in 2h, all during concurrent warmup of model-B + large batch from model-A
[alloc] slab_frag: 14%, external_free_frag: 1.2GB
```

emily: :eyes: hmm. slab fragmentation + big per-op workspace looks like the culprit. Are kernels picking the larger workspace variant under current heuristic?

rahul: Looks like it. kernel selector prefers perf-opt kernels (lower latency) even when free memory < 25% of typical workspace. We get a cascade: selector picks big kernel -> allocate_workspace fails -> runtime falls back mid-forward -> KV cache eviction/restore thrash -> OOM.

simon: Two levers: 1) prefer lower-workspace kernels when free_mem_ratio < X, 2) bump soft reservations for active model kv cache during warmup. I'd also add opportunistic buffer reuse across models to lower peak.

anya: Agree. Also noticed batching heuristic: the batcher packs requests aggressively (up to model-A's max_batch) regardless of co-residency. We could add a co-residency-aware batch cap that reduces effective max_batch when multiple models co-resident.

rahul: Proposed quick experiment: change kernel selection to use memory-aware cost = latency + alpha * workspace_bytes; alpha tunable. Also add per-model "warmup_kv_reserve" that reserves 512MB until kvcache_hit_rate>0.6.

rahul: Example config (feature-flagged):
```json
{
  "allocator": {
    "slab_compact_threshold": 0.10,
    "pooled_buffers": true,
    "buffer_reuse_tagging": true
  },
  "kernel_selector": {
    "memory_penalty_alpha": 0.00005,
    "workspace_margin_bytes": 256000000
  },
  "co_residency": {
    "soft_isolation": true,
    "per_model_kv_reserve_mb": 512,
    "batch_scale_on_coresident": 0.7
  }
}
```

emily: Love the config. buffer_reuse_tagging is key — tag buffers with model_id and reuse for compatible shapes. That should chop a lot off external_free_frag.

simon: For OOM mitigation runtime change: when allocate_workspace fails, instead of immediate fallback -> run, attempt: 1) evict cold kvcache pages up to limit 2) try pooled buffer compaction 3) select lower-workspace kernel 4) if still fail, gracefully reject with structured error + suggestion to retry smaller batch. Prefer order to avoid unnecessary perf regression.

rahul: Agreed. We'll also record telemetry: allocator.compactions, kvcache.evictions, kernel_switches_on_alloc_failure, oom_reasons. Need to ensure these are high-cardinality-tagged by model_id + route.

anya: Canary plan: enable the new allocator + kernel penalty on one dedicated node group servicing sandbox traffic for 48h. Run synthetic simultaneous warmup of model-A (heavy kv) + model-B (large weights) and compare p50/p95 latency, OOM count, and token cost.

bench-bot: bench run scheduled: canary-alloc-1965432125 started. workload: 70% model-A small chats, 30% model-B long generations.

ops-bot: alert rule created: if oom_count > 0 in 1h on canary group -> revert flag.

emily: If canary looks good, next step is incremental roll to 10% of dedicated capacity with A/B measurement on p99 tail and kvcache_hit_rate. Also create a fallback plan to disable memory_penalty_alpha if latency regresses > 5%.

simon: One more idea: prefetch-on-evict for kvcache. When we evict pages for allocator compaction, mark them with prefetch_elect score so if the same model gets scheduled soon we prefetch asynchronously (in background) to reduce hot-swapping stalls. Cost: extra PCIe traffic but may reduce 99th.

rahul: Good call. I'll add prefetch_elect to the experiment config and put up a short PR with the allocator + kernel selector change.

rahul: Action items:
- rahul: PR for kernel selector memory penalty + tests (ETA today EOD)
- emily: implement buffer_reuse_tagging prototype (ETA 2 days)
- simon: runtime OOM mitigation flow + telemetry (ETA 2 days)
- anya: run canary script + compare metrics (ETA tomorrow)

rahul: Thanks all. tagging @emily @simon @anya for visibility. :thumbsup:
